# Life of a Token — interactive simulation

**Scope:** an interactive page that follows one chat request through a small, real transformer, from the HTTP request to the stop token.
**Index:** [README](../README.md). **Builds on:** documents [00](../00-big-picture.md), [01](../01-tokenizer.md), and [03](../03-embeddings-and-positions.md) to [08](../08-inference-runtime.md).

## Open the simulation

- **Local copy:** open [`index.html`](index.html) in a browser. It needs no server and no build step. It loads `engine.js` and `toy-model.js` from the same folder.
- **Published copy:** [Life of a Token](https://claude.ai/artifact/REDACTED) (a private claude.ai artifact).

The page loads its fonts from Google Fonts. Without a network connection, it uses the system fonts.

## How to use it

1. Pick an example message, or type a message and select **Run**.
2. Select **Play**, or step with the arrow keys. Shift + right arrow jumps to the next sampled token.
3. Select a stage in the rail at the left to jump to it in the current forward pass.
4. Select any token in the context window to follow its life in the panel under the scope.
5. Change the sampler settings. The page runs the request again and stays at the same stage.

The example messages show different behaviors:

| Message | What to look at |
|---------|-----------------|
| What does the cat eat? | A one-sentence answer. In block 1, the attention of " cat" and " eats" goes back to " cat". |
| Tell me about the owl. | A three-sentence answer. The stop probability stays near 0 until the third sentence ends. |
| Tell me a fact. | An uncertain stop. After each sentence, the model gives the stop token about 50%. Change the seed to see 1, 2, or 3 sentences. |
| Pick an animal. | An uncertain choice. The model spreads the probability over 16 animals, so the sampler settings matter. |
| What does the zebra eat? | An unknown word. BPE splits " zebra" into bytes, and the model answers about a different animal with confidence. |
| Who are you? | A two-sentence fixed answer. |

## What each stage shows

| Stage | What the page shows | Document |
|-------|---------------------|----------|
| Request arrives | The HTTP request body and a summary of the run | [00](../00-big-picture.md), [08](../08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Chat template | The Llama 3 chat format around the message | [01](../01-tokenizer.md) |
| Pre-tokenizer | The chunks that the Llama 3 regex makes | [01](../01-tokenizer.md) |
| BPE merges | Each merge rule that BPE applies to each chunk | [01](../01-tokenizer.md) |
| Token IDs | The prompt IDs, next to the real Llama 3 IDs for the example messages | [01](../01-tokenizer.md) |
| Embedding lookup | The rows that the lookup copies from the embedding table | [03](../03-embeddings-and-positions.md) |
| Block *n* · Attention | The weights of each head, the causal mask, and the KV cache writes and reads | [05](../05-attention.md) |
| Block *n* · MLP | The neuron activations, and the tokens that each strong neuron pushes up | [06](../06-mlp-and-neurons.md), [13](../13-interpretability.md) |
| Output head | All logits for the last position | [07](../07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| Sampler | The value after each logit processor, and the random draw | [07](../07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| Detokenizer | Token to bytes to text, and the server-sent event | [01](../01-tokenizer.md), [08](../08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Stop check | The four stop conditions, and the stop probability at each pass | [07](../07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| Response done | The last events, the token counts, and the cost at Llama 3 8B scale | [02](../02-tensors-and-weights.md), [08](../08-inference-runtime.md) |

The attention and MLP views also show a **logit lens**: the final norm and the output head, applied to the residual stream after that block. It shows how the guess for the next token forms with depth ([nostalgebraist, 2020](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/AcKRB8wDpdaN6v6ru/interpreting-gpt-the-logit-lens)).

## The toy model

The model has the Llama layout: RMSNorm before each sub-layer, rotary positions (RoPE), grouped-query attention, a SwiGLU MLP, no bias terms, and separate embedding and output matrices.

| Setting | This model | Llama 3 8B |
|---------|------------|------------|
| Layers | 4 | 32 |
| Model dimension | 64 | 4,096 |
| Query heads / key-value heads | 4 / 2 | 32 / 8 |
| Head dimension | 16 | 128 |
| MLP neurons per layer | 224 | 14,336 |
| Vocabulary | 582: 256 bytes, 321 merges, 5 special tokens | 128,256 |
| Context window | 64 | 8,192 |
| RoPE base | 10,000 | 500,000 |
| Parameters | 296,256 | 8,030,261,248 |
| Weights | float16, 592 kB | bf16, about 16 GB |

**Tokenizer.** It is a byte-level BPE tokenizer. It uses the Llama 3 pre-tokenizer regex and the five Llama 3 chat-format tokens, so the prompt has the same layout as a real Llama 3 prompt. The training text has 145 distinct chunks, and the tokenizer merges until each of them is one token.

**Training data.** The script samples 60,000 chat transcripts from templates about 16 animals:

- one fact per question: the sound, the food, the home, or the number of legs,
- "Tell me about the …": three facts in a fixed order,
- "Pick an animal.": a uniform random animal,
- "Tell me a fact.": one to three random facts, with a 50% stop after the first,
- small talk: greetings, thanks, and "Who are you?".

About one question in five starts with a lower-case letter, and about one in seven has no final punctuation.

**Training.** 3,000 steps of AdamW with a batch of 64 and a cosine learning-rate schedule. It takes about one minute on a laptop CPU. The final loss is about 0.3. Most of that loss comes from text that no model can predict, such as the random animal or the next question.

**Checks.** After the training, the script rounds the weights to float16 and decodes all 152 template questions with greedy sampling. All 152 answers are correct. `check_engine.js` then confirms that the JavaScript engine gives the same logits as PyTorch, within 5 × 10⁻⁵.

## What is real and what is simplified

Real:

- Every number on the page comes from the model. Nothing is scripted.
- The tokenizer, the chat template, and the special tokens follow Llama 3.
- The sampler applies the processors in the order of Hugging Face transformers: repetition penalty, temperature, top-k, top-p, then the random draw.
- The stop rules are those of a typical OpenAI-compatible server: a stop token, a stop sequence, the token limit, and the context window.

Simplified:

- The page runs one request on the CPU. A real server batches many requests on GPUs and keeps the KV cache in pages ([08](../08-inference-runtime.md)).
- The engine feeds the prompt one position at a time. This gives the same values as one parallel prefill pass, but it is slower.
- The engine computes in 64-bit floats. A real server computes in bf16 or in fewer bits.
- The stop-sequence check does not hold back text that can start a stop sequence. Some servers do.
- The logit lens is a rough tool. [Belrose et al. (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08112) found it unreliable for some models.
- The neuron table shows only the direct effect of a neuron on the logits, as in [Geva et al. (2022)](https://aclanthology.org/2022.emnlp-main.3). It ignores the effect through later layers.
- The Llama 3 8B values are calculations from its configuration, not measurements. The decode time uses the rough 2 TB/s memory bandwidth from [08](../08-inference-runtime.md).

## Files

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `index.html` | The page: layout, styles, and the code for each stage view. |
| `engine.js` | The tokenizer, the transformer, the sampler, and the serving loop. It has no dependencies and runs in a browser or in Node. |
| `toy-model.js` | Generated. The configuration, the merge rules, the float16 weights in base64, and reference outputs from PyTorch. |
| `train/train_toy_model.py` | Builds the corpus, trains the tokenizer and the model, checks the answers, and writes `toy-model.js`. |
| `train/check_engine.js` | Compares `engine.js` with the PyTorch reference in `toy-model.js`. |
| `train/requirements.txt` | The Python packages for the training script. |

## Rebuild the model

Run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r simulation/train/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python simulation/train/train_toy_model.py
node simulation/train/check_engine.js
```

A rebuild on another machine can give slightly different weights, because CPU training is not bit-for-bit reproducible. Then a seed can give a different sampled reply.

## Sources

[sources.md](../sources.md) lists the sources of the simulation and the web searches that supported it, in the section "Token lifecycle simulation".

# LLM Internals — A System Architecture View

This branch collects research on the inner components of a large language model (LLM).
The documents explain each component as a part of a system: what it receives, what it produces, what state it keeps, and what it costs.
The documents avoid the math. When a formula matters, the documents describe its effect, not its derivation.

## Scope

- **In scope:** decoder-only transformer LLMs (the GPT, Llama, Mistral, and Claude family of designs), from text input to text output, plus the runtime that serves them.
- **Out of scope:** the math of backpropagation, image and audio models, and product-level topics such as prompt design.

## Reading order

Read the documents in number order for a full walk through the request path. Each document also stands alone.

| # | Document | Question it answers |
|---|----------|---------------------|
| 00 | [The big picture](00-big-picture.md) | What are the parts of an LLM, and how does a request flow through them? |

| 07 | [Output head and sampling](07-output-and-sampling.md) | How does a vector become the next token? |
| 08 | [Inference runtime](08-inference-runtime.md) | How does a server run the model fast: prefill, decode, KV cache, batches? |
| 09 | [Scaling across devices](09-scaling-across-devices.md) | How does a model that is too big for one GPU run on many? |
| 10 | [Mixture of experts](10-mixture-of-experts.md) | How do some models use only part of their weights for each token? |

# Glossary

One-line definitions for the terms in this document set. The number in brackets points to the document that explains the term.

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Activation function | A fixed non-linear function inside the MLP, for example SiLU or GELU. [06](06-mlp-and-neurons.md) |
| Activation | An intermediate value that the model computes during a forward pass. [02](02-tensors-and-weights.md) |
| Attention head | One of many parallel, independent attention lookups inside a layer. [05](05-attention.md) |
| Attention | The sub-layer that moves information between token positions. [05](05-attention.md) |
| Attribution graph | A traced graph of the features that caused one output. [13](13-interpretability.md) |
| Autoregressive generation | The loop that predicts one token, appends it, and predicts again. [00](00-big-picture.md) |
| Base model | The model after pretraining and before instruction tuning. [12](12-training-lifecycle.md) |
| bfloat16 (bf16) | A 16-bit number format with the same range as float32. [02](02-tensors-and-weights.md) |
| Block (layer) | One repeated unit of the stack: attention plus MLP, with norms and residual additions. [04](04-transformer-block.md) |
| BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding) | A tokenizer algorithm that merges frequent adjacent pairs into new tokens. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |
| Causal mask | The rule that a token can attend only to itself and earlier tokens. [05](05-attention.md) |
| Chain of thought (CoT) | Intermediate reasoning tokens that a model writes before its final answer. [14](14-reasoning-models.md) |
| Chat template | A Jinja template that converts chat messages into one token sequence. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |
| Circuit | A sub-graph of features and weights that implements one behavior. [13](13-interpretability.md) |
| Context window | The maximum number of tokens the model accepts in one sequence. [03](03-embeddings-and-positions.md) |
| Continuous batching | A scheduler that adds and removes requests after every decode step. [08](08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Decode | The phase that generates output tokens one at a time. Memory-bound. [08](08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Detokenizer | The function that converts token IDs back to text. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |
| Distillation | Fine-tuning a small model on outputs, such as reasoning chains, from a large model. [14](14-reasoning-models.md) |
| dtype | The number format of a tensor's elements. [02](02-tensors-and-weights.md) |
| Embedding table | The weight matrix that maps each token ID to a vector. [03](03-embeddings-and-positions.md) |
| Expert | One of many MLPs in a mixture-of-experts layer. [10](10-mixture-of-experts.md) |
| Feature | A meaningful direction in activation space. Not the same as a neuron. [13](13-interpretability.md) |
| FlashAttention | An exact attention implementation that reduces GPU memory traffic. [05](05-attention.md) |
| GGUF | The single-file model format of llama.cpp. [11](11-model-files-and-quantization.md) |
| GQA (grouped-query attention) | Attention in which groups of query heads share one key/value head. [05](05-attention.md) |
| GRPO | An RL method that compares each attempt with the average of a group of attempts for the same problem. [14](14-reasoning-models.md) |
| Induction head | An attention circuit that finds an earlier copy of the current token and predicts what followed it. [05](05-attention.md) |
| KV cache | Saved attention keys and values of earlier tokens, reused at each decode step. [08](08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Logit | The raw score that the output head gives to one vocabulary entry. [07](07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| LoRA | Small add-on matrices that fine-tune a frozen model. [12](12-training-lifecycle.md) |
| MLP (feed-forward network) | The sub-layer that transforms each token vector alone. [06](06-mlp-and-neurons.md) |
| Model dimension (d_model) | The length of each token vector in the residual stream. [04](04-transformer-block.md) |
| MoE (mixture of experts) | A design in which a router sends each token to a few of many experts. [10](10-mixture-of-experts.md) |
| Neuron | One hidden unit of an MLP layer: a read vector, an activation function, and a write vector. [06](06-mlp-and-neurons.md) |
| Output head (LM head, unembedding) | The matrix that converts the final vector into one logit per vocabulary entry. [07](07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| PagedAttention | KV cache management with fixed-size blocks, like OS memory pages. [08](08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Parameter (weight) | One learned number in the model. [02](02-tensors-and-weights.md) |
| Pipeline parallelism | A split that puts different blocks on different GPUs. [09](09-scaling-across-devices.md) |
| Polysemantic neuron | A neuron that responds to several unrelated features. [13](13-interpretability.md) |
| Prefill | The phase that processes the whole prompt in one pass. Compute-bound. [08](08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Quantization | Storage of numbers in fewer bits, with scale factors. [11](11-model-files-and-quantization.md) |
| Reasoning model | A model trained with RL to write a long chain of thought before it answers. [14](14-reasoning-models.md) |
| Residual stream | The shared vector per token that every layer reads from and adds to. [04](04-transformer-block.md) |
| RLHF | Reinforcement learning from human feedback: tuning with a reward model trained on human rankings. [12](12-training-lifecycle.md) |
| RLVR | Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards: a program, not a person, checks the answer. [14](14-reasoning-models.md) |
| RMSNorm | A normalization that rescales a vector by its root-mean-square size. [04](04-transformer-block.md) |
| RoPE | Rotary position embedding: a position-dependent rotation of queries and keys. [03](03-embeddings-and-positions.md) |
| Router | The small layer in an MoE block that picks experts for each token. [10](10-mixture-of-experts.md) |
| safetensors | A weight file format with a JSON header and raw data, and no executable code. [11](11-model-files-and-quantization.md) |
| Sampler | The runtime policy that picks one token from the logits. [07](07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| Sparse autoencoder (SAE) | A helper network that decomposes activations into interpretable features. [13](13-interpretability.md) |
| Special token | A vocabulary entry with a control meaning, such as end-of-sequence. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |
| Speculative decoding | A small model proposes tokens, and the large model verifies them in one pass. [08](08-inference-runtime.md) |
| Superposition | The storage of more features than dimensions in overlapping directions. [13](13-interpretability.md) |
| SwiGLU | A gated MLP variant with three matrices: gate, up, and down. [06](06-mlp-and-neurons.md) |
| Temperature | A sampler setting that sharpens or flattens the probability distribution. [07](07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| Tensor parallelism | A split of each weight matrix across GPUs. [09](09-scaling-across-devices.md) |
| Tensor | A multi-dimensional array of numbers with a dtype, shape, and device. [02](02-tensors-and-weights.md) |
| Test-time compute | Extra inference work, such as longer chains or more samples, spent to improve an answer. [14](14-reasoning-models.md) |
| Token | A unit of text that the tokenizer maps to one integer ID. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |
| Tokenizer | The component that converts text to token IDs and back. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |
| Top-k / top-p | Sampler filters that keep only the most probable tokens. [07](07-output-and-sampling.md) |
| Vocabulary | The fixed set of all tokens that a tokenizer can produce. [01](01-tokenizer.md) |

## Token lifecycle simulation

The [simulation](simulation/README.md) builds on documents 00 to 08. The research for it on 2026-10-21 looked for the exact details that a working model and runtime need: the Llama 3 chat format and its token IDs, the order of the logit processors, the stop rules, and two interpretability methods that the page shows.

Unlike in the first research round, direct fetches from GitHub, docs.vllm.ai, and huggingface.co worked.

### Search log

| # | Search or fetch | What it confirmed | Used for |
|---|-----------------|-------------------|----------|
| 1 | Web search: `Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct config.json vocab_size 128256 rope_theta 500000 num_key_value_heads 8 intermediate_size 14336` | Community copies of the config agree on these values. No official copy was in the results, so fetch 11 checked them. | Llama 3 8B column of the comparison table |
| 2 | Web search: `Llama 3 prompt format special tokens begin_of_text start_header_id end_header_id eot_id 128009 generation_config eos_token_id` | Meta's prompt-format page gives the role of each special token. It gives no token IDs. | Chat template stage |
| 3 | Web search: `llama3 tokenizer.py pat_str regex …` | torchtune and llama.cpp use the same pre-tokenizer pattern. The upstream file was not in the results, so fetch 8 read it. | Pre-tokenizer stage |
| 4 | Web search: `Hugging Face transformers generate logits processor order repetition penalty temperature top_k top_p` | No clear answer. Fetch 10 read the source code. | Sampler stage |
| 5 | Web search: `vLLM sampler order penalties temperature top-k top-p min-p` | The vLLM `Sampler` documentation lists the order. Fetch 9 read the full list. | Sampler stage |
| 6 | Web search: `CTRL Keskar 2019 repetition penalty discount logits of previously generated tokens penalty 1.2` | CTRL introduced "penalized sampling": a factor θ on the logits of earlier tokens, with θ ≈ 1.2. | Repetition penalty setting |
| 7 | Web search: `OpenAI chat completions finish_reason "stop" "length" natural stop point or stop sequence max_tokens` | `"stop"` means a natural stop or a stop sequence. `"length"` means the token limit. | Stop check and final event |
| 8 | Fetch: `raw.githubusercontent.com/meta-llama/llama3/main/llama/tokenizer.py` | The full pattern. The special-token list, with ID = 128,000 + list index. Stop tokens `<\|end_of_text\|>` and `<\|eot_id\|>`. The `ChatFormat` code. | Tokenizer and template of the toy model |
| 9 | Fetch: `docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/v1/sample/sampler/` | Order: allowed-token and bad-word masks, other logit processors, penalties, then temperature, min-p, top-k and top-p, and the draw. | Note in the sampler stage |
| 10 | Fetch: `raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/transformers/main/src/transformers/generation/utils.py` | `_get_logits_processor` adds `RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor` before the warpers. The warpers run in this order: temperature, top-h, top-k, top-p, min-p. | Order of the sampler in `engine.js` |
| 11 | Download: `tokenizer.json`, `config.json`, and `generation_config.json` from the `NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct` mirror | `vocab_size` 128,256, `rope_theta` 500,000, `max_position_embeddings` 8,192, `tie_word_embeddings` false. `eos_token_id` [128001, 128009], `temperature` 0.6, `top_p` 0.9. content.text:
I built the simulation in `simulation/`. It runs a small, real Llama-style transformer in the browser and steps through one chat request, from the HTTP request to the stop token.

**Open it**
- **Local:** open `simulation/index.html` in a browser. It needs no server and no build step.
- **Published copy:** [Life of a Token](https://claude.ai/artifact/REDACTED). It is private, so other people cannot open it until you share it.

**What it shows**
- **Stages:** request, chat template, pre-tokenizer, BPE merges, token IDs, embedding lookup, then attention and MLP in each of the 4 blocks, output head, sampler, detokenizer, and stop check.
- **Loop:** the forward pass repeats once per token until the model samples `<|eot_id|>`.
- **Token panel:** you can select any token and follow it: where it came from, its KV cache entry, the later tokens that read it, and when the cache is freed.
- **Links and scale:** each stage links to its research document on GitHub and shows the Llama 3 8B figures. Those figures are calculated from the model's config, not measured.

**The model**
I trained the model in this session. It has 296,256 parameters and trained in about one minute on the CPU. It knows facts about 16 animals, and it uses the Llama 3 pre-tokenizer pattern, chat template and special tokens.

Every number on the page comes from the model, not a script. Two of the example messages show the sampler at work:
- **"Tell me a fact."** After the first sentence, the model gives the stop token about 50%, so the seed decides when the reply ends.
- **"Pick an animal."** The model spreads its probability over all 16 animals.

**Checks**
- `node simulation/train/check_engine.js` passes. The JavaScript scores match PyTorch to within 5 × 10⁻⁵.
- With greedy decoding, the model answers all 152 template questions correctly.
- In a headless browser, all six example messages and the edge cases ran through every step with no errors. The edge cases were greedy, top-k, repetition penalty, max tokens, a stop sequence, and a prompt too long for the context window.
- The page has no sideways scroll at 400 px width, and both light and dark mode render.

**What I recorded**
- `sources.md` has a new section, "Token lifecycle simulation". It logs 9 web searches, 3 page fetches and 1 file download, and adds 10 sources with a trust tier for each.
- `glossary.md` has 4 new terms, and `README.md` links to the simulation.
- `simulation/README.md` explains the model, what is simplified, and how to rebuild the model.

**Notes**
- I did not commit. The changes are on `llm-research`: 3 changed files and the new `simulation/` folder.
- The published copy is the same page without the outer HTML tags, because the artifact host adds its own. I saved the steps to republish it in my memory notes for this repo.

Sources:
- [meta-llama/llama3 tokenizer.py](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama3/blob/main/llama/tokenizer.py)
- [Meta Llama 3 prompt format](https://www.llama.com/docs/model-cards-and-prompt-formats/meta-llama-3/)
- [Llama 3 8B Instruct config files (community mirror)](https://huggingface.co/NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct)
- [Hugging Face transformers generation/utils.py](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/generation/utils.py)
- [vLLM Sampler documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/v1/sample/sampler/)
- [Keskar et al., CTRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05858)
- [OpenAI completion object (finish_reason)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/completions/object)
- [nostalgebraist, the logit lens](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/AcKRB8wDpdaN6v6ru/interpreting-gpt-the-logit-lens)
- [Belrose et al., Tuned Lens](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08112)
- [Geva et al., EMNLP 2022](https://aclanthology.org/2022.emnlp-main.3)
